game.title: Ys Memoire: The Oath in Felghana

entries.source_text: Fine mess we've got here in Felghana、\nno?
Chester's the big shocker、 for me.\nHe's had a dignified air about him ever\nsince he was a child.
We always suspected that he might be the\nson of a nobleman、 or some such thing.\nBut there's nothing noble about McGuire!
Dogi、 on the other hand、 was a total\nmess as a child...and look at HIM\nnow!
...Though I suppose I can't really\ncompare、 since I know nothing at all\nabout Chester's life before Redmont.
The events of his distant past could\nhold the missing puzzle piece that\ngives valid context to all his actions.
...But then、 what do I know? The more I\nthink about it、 the more I realize just\nhow pointless it is to think about it!
I'm uninvolved in the proceedings、 and I\nhave no skills to contribute to them. But\nyou do! So I'd like you to have this.
We often find pieces of raval on the\nfloor during cleanup. Dragged in on the\nminers' shoes、 no doubt.
It's not much、 but I do hope it can be\nof some use to you.
Really、 it's about the only thing I can\ndo to help、 I'm afraid. After all、 I'm\nbasically just here to look pretty!
Huh?!
H-hey、 Red... Can I see that ring you\ngot there?
That's my ring、 all right. I'd recognize\nit anywhere!
C-c'mon、 man、 help a guy out! Let me\nhave it back、 will ya'?
Oh、 man、 thank you! I seriously owe you\none! You're the best、 Red!
In fact、 you know what? I've got\nsomething I'd like to give you、\nto show my appreciation.
Now I can go back home to my family、 and\nthey won't bite my head off!
All riiiight! I am so ready for anything\nnow!
The hell、 man?! Geez、 what am I supposed\nto do now? Can't go home without that\nring!
All right、 now I can fight for the town\nwithout any worries!
Then、 I can go right back home to my\nfamily in Garman!
Hi、 Adol. Isn't it a bit early to be\nsetting off?
Are you sure we can't convince you to\nstay a little longer?
Come on、 now... You're going to make him\nfeel guilty about leaving!
Well、 he'll be missed! It'll be lonely\naround here without him、 for sure.
...I know!
Maybe you can stay here、 and Dogi can\ngo off on some grand adventure in your\nplace!
Aww、 Mams、 why you gotta bust my walls\nlike that?!
Ahh、 I'm just teasing.
Adol、 I sincerely hope I have a chance\nto see you again. You'll always be\nwelcome in Redmont!
And if you DO come back、 I'll make you\none hell of a feast to celebrate!
So、 Adol... You're leaving us、 then?
We are all greatly in your debt. Thank\nyou for everything you've done.
What about you、 Master? What are you\ngonna do now?
Planning to go back to your cabin up in\nthe mountains?
No、 now that Count McGuire has reformed、\nI see no further need to live the life\nof a hermit.
And with the monsters gone、 I'm left\nadrift in this world; a man without a\npurpose...
Oh、 come now、 Master、 you're no such\nthing!
No、 I am. My job here is done. All I'm\nqualified for is mercenary work、 and\nthat's...out of the question.
Honestly、 I think I'm just going to\nrelax now. Relax、 and mourn the loss\nof a dear pupil、 of course...
I see it as retirement. Living out the\nrest of my days here、 helping to re-\nbuild... I actually look forward to it.
So Adol、 while I'm here、 I think I'm\ngoing to swing by the Elderm Mountains\nfor a bit、 to visit my old master.
He's the one who taught me everything I\nknow about fighting、 back when I was a\nkid.
If anyone would know the reason for all\nthe monsters showing up around here、\nhe'd be the one.
I won't be gone long、 though. You should\nrelax、 and tour the town. It's a really\nnice place!
If you have any questions、 you can ask\nElena.
She said her house was on the outskirts\nof town、 so I'm sure it won't be too\ntough to find.
I'm off for now. See you later、 buddy!
Dogi?!
I can't believe it...\nIt's really you!\nMy little nightmare's come home!
And look at those muscles! You've grown\nso BIG! Last time I saw you、 you were\njust a pudgy little brat!
Heh... Yeah、 it's me. I'm back...
You're looking well!
You know、 I haven't heard a peep out of\nyou since you left...
Would it be so much to ask for some kind\nof contact? A letter、 at least、 if you\ncouldn't visit!
Aww、 I'm sorry、 Mams.
Well、 I always figured you'd do well for\nyourself.
It certainly is nice to see you back\nsafely、 though.
And you're...a friend of Dogi's、 then?
I see. Well、 thank you for looking after\nour little wayward wanderer.
Unfortunately、 you've arrived at a\npretty bad time. Lots of unpleasant\nbusiness going on、 lately.
But still...happy events like these are\nrare、 so I intend to enjoy this while I\ncan!
Mams...
You two boys must be hungry.
Let me fix you up a nice、 big meal...\nand you'd better clean your plates、 if\nyou know what's good for you!
...Hmm?
Hey... Can I see that hammer for a sec?
Oh、 man、 I can feel it...\nThis baby's just packed with power!
...Where the hell did you find something\nlike this?!
Genos Island...?!
Huh... Guess there's some truth to the\nrumors about that place after all!
Using this hammer's energy、 I can easily\ntemper raval ore without damaging it--\nand you have no idea how big that is!
I could probably make you a hell of a\nshield with it、 if I had the materials.
But that's just it. I'd need...a LOT of\nraval ore.
Probably somewhere around 1000 rocks...
...Wait... You already have a thousand\nhunks of raval ore? ...Seriously?!
Well、 damn、 color me impressed...\nHow'd you manage to get so much?\nAnd...where were you keeping it?!
Either way、 I can get started right now、\nif you want. No time like the present、\nand I'm itching to try out that hammer!
Yeah、 not exactly an amount you can\nreasonably expect someone to get their\nhands on!
Well、 if you do happen to find yourself\nwith more raval ore than you know what\nto do with、 my offer stands.
Just say the word.
Supposedly、 there's a way of working on\nraval without damaging it or diluting\nits energy. Perfect-quality smithing...
If only I knew the secret、 I'm confident\nI could pull it off、 and make you the\nshield of your dreams!
...Thing is、 there are two big\nobstacles standing in my way.
First off、 I need more raval ore than\nthe miners bring back in a month...and\nthat's a month when the quarry's OPEN.
Plus、 like I said、 when you pound raval、\nyou damage it. It's a soft mineral by\nnature、 so there ain't no way around it!
I learned the craft from my grandfather、\nthough、 and he learned it from the\nmasters on Genos Island.
And from all the stories he used to\ntell、 I bet the miracle-workers over\nthere knew how to do it...

People been talkin'. Sounds like you're\none tough customer!

I can tell by your equipment that you're\nno slouch. Definitely seems like you\ntake good care of your armaments.

...I like you、 man. You're clearly the\nreal deal. If you ever need any weapons\nor armor tempered、 you just let me know.

I'll have to charge you a service fee\ntoo、 though、 or else Cynthia's gonna put\nup a fuss like you wouldn't believe.

Might've even outdone myself...
I'd probably even go so far as to say\nit's the best piece of work I've ever\nproduced!
Just make sure you put it to good use、\nokay?
...You sure?
Well、 if you should ever change your\nmind、 you know where I'll be. I mean、\nI pretty much never leave this spot!

So Bishop Nikolas was the puppetmaster\nbehind this whole ordeal...
...I... I just can't believe it's true!
He was always such a devoted proponent\nof God's teachings...
But the facts are the facts...and this\nis no time to wallow in disillusionment.
Not only has Elena been taken、 but that\nearthquake's brought us new monsters、\nthe likes of which we've never seen.
Galbalan's resurrection is indeed nigh.\nThe warning signs are all here.
Redmont...cannot survive much more of\nthis.
...Dear Lord、 hear my prayer...
...Let's not bother God just yet. Man's\ntime is far from over!
...Berhardt? What in the world are you\ndoing here?!
It's been a long time、 Mayor.
I spoke with McGuire at the inn. He\nfilled me in on the situation、 more or\nless.
Thought I might lend my strength to the\ntown's defenses.
That would be most appreciated. With you\nhere、 we'll be able to stand our ground\nfor as long as it takes!
Is there anything you need for the job?
Just for every able-bodied man to join\nthe fray.
And Father Pierre、 I'd like for you to\ngather the women and children、 and make\nsure they're safe in the church.
Understood!
I'll get right on it!
...Now then、 Adol.
If you're to set off for Genos Island、\nthere's that dock north of the town\nentrance、 along the road to the castle.
Wait... Are you...?
You and Dogi came here on a small boat、\ncorrect?
The island's not far off shore. You can\nsee it from the dock、 and should be able\nto reach it easily.
Now、 wait just one second!
Elena may have been kidnapped、 but you\ncan't seriously be thinking of asking\nAdol to--
Mayor、 this young man has been guided\ndown the path of Genos himself.
Ultimately、 it is his choice whether or\nnot to go. But you know as well as I do\nwhich option he'll take.
We mustn't hold him back. All we can do\nis give him our support.
...Time is precious.
I'll start bolstering the town's\ndefenses.
Oh、 and Adol...
Chester's in the room next door. He\nawoke shortly after I arrived here.
I believe he has something he'd like to\nsay to you. Before you go、 you may wish\nto pay him a visit.
I had no idea Chester was hiding a\nsecret like that all this time...
He lived under my roof for ten years、\nand never once did I question where he\ncame from、 or how much he remembered...
I feel like such a fool...
Please don't blame yourself、 Mayor.
Right now、 we need to focus on the\nmatter at hand. We need to focus on\nValestein Castle.
What we know is that Chester is planning\nto take his revenge through the power\ncontained in those statues...
The question is、 are those statues in\nsome way responsible for the lifeless、\nsoulless appearance of our attackers?
It seems that way...
I think now would be a good time to get\nin touch with Bishop Nikolas at the\ncastle...
<scale:1.2>E-excuse me!
Sister? What's wrong? You're white as\na ghost!
The soldiers haven't returned、 have\nthey?!
N-no...
It's just that... I haven't seen Elena\nfor some time now、 and when I asked the\nchildren where she went...
...It seems she's left town again!
What?!
Well that's...not good.
She must have heard about Chester、 and\ngone to Valestein Castle...
Yes、 I think that's a safe assumption.
...It's an awfully rash thing to do、\nthough、 even for her...
Dear me...
...Adol、 I'm sorry to ask...
...But won't you please find Elena and\nbring her home to us?
I can't bear to think of what might\nhappen to her out there...
You'll do it? Thank you、 Adol!\nThank you so very much!
We're truly in your debt、 Adol.
I hate that we've been such a burden to\nyou since your arrival here. I can't\nimagine what you must think of us!
Godspeed on your journey.
I will pray for your health and success.\nBest of luck to you、 Adol.
Ohh、 Adol!
Adol! You made it!
Pierre just got back from the castle a\nlittle while ago.
Seems Bishop Nikolas made a good case\non his behalf、 and the count saw fit to\nlet him go.
Yes、 he spoke far kinder things of me\nthan I deserve. I owe him a tremendous\ndebt of gratitude.
Unfortunately、 Chester was out on an\nerrand for the count at the time、 so no\nanswers were to be had on that front.
And the bishop had no luck finding any\ninformation on the statues、 either、 I'm\nafraid...
That is unfortunate...
...But、 we shall take the victories we\ncan get. And the bishop IS still there、\nso answers may yet be forthcoming.
On another note...
...Did you happen to find anything else\nupon your return to the abandoned mine、\nAdol?
On another note...
How did your investigation of the\nabandoned mine go、 Adol?
Amazing... You're like a magnet for\ndanger!
Hmm... Genos...and Galbalan!
I never thought I'd hear that name\nagain、 much less in this context...
You know what it is、 then?
It's an old local legend.
Long ago、 a great and terrible beast\nknown as Galbalan came from across the\nsea、 and took control of Felghana.
He had the power to transform the people\nand spirits under his influence into\ntwisted、 evil creatures-- or so it goes.
But one day、 a hero appeared、 wielding a\nmighty sword.
He was the warrior、 Genos...
He borrowed the powers of the gods、 and\nfought the beast...and at long last、\nagainst insurmountable odds、 he won.
...And that's about the extent of what I\nknow、 I'm afraid.
Legends like that aren't too popular\nthese days. Barely anyone remembers\nthem、 save for old coots like me!
I've certainly never heard it before...
But that does remind me、 I asked Bishop\nNikolas earlier if he happened to know\nthe origin of the Illburns Ruins.
Apparently、 it used to be a church of\nsorts、 devoted to some long-lost pagan\ndeity.
Interesting. Given the circumstances of\nlate、 it's not unreasonable to suspect\nthere may be a connection.
There's also one more thing that bears\nmentioning.
Out in the Sienna Bay、 there's an old、\ndeserted island we've always known by\njust one name... Genos Island.
There was once a small village there、\nbut it was ravaged and destroyed by\ndisease twelve years ago.
...What?!
It happened three years before you\narrived、 so I'm not surprised you\nwouldn't know about it.
Genos Village never had many dealings\nwith Redmont、 and the whole tragedy was\nso terrible、 people rarely discuss it.
I don't know much about the disease that\nkilled them all、 though、 I'm afraid.
According to the official statement from\nValestein Castle、 it was some sort of\nextremely severe fever...
This doesn't instill a lot of hope. An\nisland named for the hero who defeated\nGalbalan、 totally annihilated...
The voice Adol heard is seeming less and\nless implausible、 and more and more...\nfrightening...
Indeed...
...Adol.
Dogi's gone to speak with his master、\nBerhardt. Perhaps you should meet\nwith Berhardt as well.
He's a rather eccentric man who's chosen\na life of near-solitude、 and devoted\nhimself to studying the land's folklore.
There's no one in Felghana who'd be more\nlikely to know about Genos、 Galbalan、\nthe statues and maybe even that voice.
I believe I'll return to the castle and\nupdate Bishop Nikolas on what we've\ndiscussed here.
If you decide to follow Dogi、 Adol、 I\nsuggest you exercise caution. The Elderm\nMountains are...not hospitable.
I still can't believe what happened at\nthe ruins...
I just... I mean、 what can Chester\npossibly be thinking?
Mayor、 I hate to say this、 but we have\nlarger concerns at the moment.
The closure of the quarry is bad enough、\nbut to threaten a priest on top of it\nall...
Chester's a factor、 yes、 but I think our\nfirst priority should be McGuire. He is\nindisputably the root of our problems.
Yes... You're right、 of course.
Bishop Nikolas、 do you have any inkling\nas to what Count McGuire may be after?
I'm afraid not...but then、 he's never\nbeen one to talk openly about his\naffairs.
His wife and their two children attend\nmorning mass without him、 always.
I do find it hard to believe、 though、\nthat he'd try and claim authority\nbeyond that of the church.
What would you suggest we do about\nFather Pierre、 then?
As head of the Felghana diocese、 it is\nmy duty to oversee the well-being of all\nmembers of the clergy.
When I return to the castle、 I intend to\nhave a talk with the count.
Fear not... I should be able to secure\nFather Pierre's release.
Much obliged、 on that.
...I'll leave Father Pierre to you、\nthen. Thank you.
I must say、 though、 I am a bit concerned\nabout these statues Count McGuire has\nChester searching for.
May we see the two you've found thus\nfar、 Adol?
Interesting...and very unique...
So the big critters were guarding\nthese?
Hmm... I sense an unusual power from\nwithin them.
It's possible there may be a link\nbetween these statues and the recent\nmonster appearances...
Wh-what?
How do you figure?
Well、 this is pure conjecture on my\npart...
But these two come from the quarry and\nthe ruins、 both of which seem to be\nhotbeds for monster activity as of late.
And each was guarded by a large\ncreature of unusual strength...
Does that not strike you as more than\nmere coincidence?
Hmm、 you may be right...
And if that's the case、 we'd be\nespecially foolish to let the count\nget his hands on them!
I think we should safeguard them until\nwe know exactly what's happening.
What's wrong、 Dewey?
Oh、 nothing...
I just get the feeling I've seen these\nstatues somewhere before...
Wh-what?!
C'mon... Out with it、 Dewey!
...I'm thinking、 I'm thinking...\nIt's not like this was just yesterday...
It was...down inside the old abandoned\nmine、 if I recall correctly. There was a\nmural painted on the wall...
Abandoned mine...?
It's an old、 deep section of the Tigray\nQuarry that we exhausted long ago. Been\nclosed off ever since.
We found a really ornate mural painted\non one of the walls there. Can't even\nimagine how old it was.
But if memory serves、 it depicted four\nstatues that looked an awful lot like\nthe ones we've got here...
Could...there really be a connection?
Hmm... Well、 it certainly warrants\nan investigation...
...All right!
Hey Adol、 what say we split our efforts?
I think I have an idea.
I'll get my stuff together and return to\nthe Elderm Mountains、 while you head to\nthe abandoned mine.
Ahh... You intend to see Berhardt!
Yeah、 the old master.
He knows more about Felghana's legends\nand folklore than anyone else、 so he can\nprobably fill in some of the blanks.
...Plus、 he might know something about\nChester's situation.
He was Chester's master、 too、 after all.
He might have some idea why that idiot's\nbeen acting like such a jackass.
I'll speak with Chester directly、 at the\ncastle. He may be more likely to grant\nFather Pierre's release than McGuire.
I'll also see if I can learn anything\npertinent about the statues、 while I'm\nthere.
Sounds like a plan. Hope you can talk\nyour way through that thick skull of\nhis!
Adol、 I'll catch you later. Good luck in\nthe abandoned mine. Don't get yourself\nkilled without me、 you got it?
If you have a chance、 too、 be sure to\ncheck in on Elena.
I feel so bad for her...poor kid...\nLet's make sure we get this all sorted\nout、 for her sake!
...All right、 Adol.
The entrance to the abandoned mine is\nnext to the quarry's storehouse、 at the\nbottom of that first vertical shaft.
I'll go on ahead and get the door open、\nsince the lock's kinda tricky. Get your\nstuff together and meet me there、 okay?
Are you sure that's wise、 Dewey?
Monsters aside、 remember、 the quarry's\noff-limits right now. If McGuire's men\ncatch you there...
It won't be a problem. I'll bring Paul\nand Ricardo for manpower、 and we'll be\nin and out before anyone's the wiser.
Got it、 Adol? Don't keep us waiting!\nYou know where we'll be、 so hurry up!
Count McGuire is the lord of Felghana、\nthough he's not native to this land.\nHe's actually from Romn.
From the moment he took power here、 he\nlevied exorbitantly high taxes and\npressured us into forced labor.
Then、 a few days ago、 he ordered us to\nshut down Tigray Quarry-- the town's\nprimary source of income!

Do you know the name Adol Christin?
Ah、 Adol Christin...
He was a swordsman and adventurer born over\na thousand years ago in a small mountain\nvillage in northeastern Europe.
From his boyhood days to his final years、 he\nsurrendered each and every moment of his life\nto fate、 always looking for a new adventure.
Tales of his exploits can be found in the\nhistories of almost every world culture--\nthough interpretations do vary quite wildly.
For every record that identifies him as a\njust and virtuous hero、 there is another that\nbrands him an emissary of chaos and disorder.
Were these divergent accounts the only\nreferences available、 it would be most diffi-\ncult to paint an accurate picture of the man.
Fortunately、 there are other、 far more\nreliable sources of information on the\nlife and times of Adol Christin.
I speak、 of course、 of his own personal\ntravelogues、 which number well over one\nhundred.
His many adventures have been meticulously\nchronicled therein、 thoroughly detailing\nevery person、 place and event of note.
These are not tall tales、 but factual\naccounts.
Each volume is comprised of a simple、 honest\nnarrative、 with an emotional detachment that\nwelcomes personal interpretation.
Yet despite Adol's dry and humble candor、 all\nwho read of these brave new worlds come away\nfrom the experience deeply affected.
Indeed、 'tis as if the reader is right there\nwith him、 feeling just as he must have felt.
The events I shall now recount took place a\nmere three years after Adol Christin set out\non his first adventure.
Collectively、 these accounts are regarded by\nscholars as the ［Felghana Archives］.
I invite you to take up Adol's sword as if it\nwere your own、 and allow yourself to become\nimmersed within his words...
Our story begins with two travelers standing\natop a hill overlooking the ocean.
As they stood、 the breeze from Sienna Bay\nwashed over them、 bringing with it the salty\nscents of the sea.
These sights and sounds and smells all mixed\ntogether to create a sense of wonderment、\nreinvigorating their travel-wearied hearts.
The younger of the two men stood transfixed、\nstaring at the beautiful scenery in front of\nhim. His eyes glinted with vigor and promise.
The wind tussled his hair、 and pulled at\nhis clothes like an eager pet greeting its\nmaster.
One could scarcely be certain which was\nbrighter: the sun in the sky、 or the fiery\nred locks of a man longing for new frontiers.
Needless to say、 this was Adol Christin、\nwhose name was already widely renowned\nfrom his prior adventures.
At the time of our tale、 Adol was 19 years\nold、 placing him on the very cusp of boyhood\nand manhood.
His traveling companion was notably older in\nappearance.
He was a buff、 burly man with impossible\nmuscles、 around the age of 24 or 25. This\nwas、 of course、 the former thief、 Dogi.
Adol's life was once saved by Dogi、 and the\ntwo of them became inseparable ever since.
They were like kindred spirits、 and had\njourneyed together for around two years\nat this point.
One might call them wanderers、 for they would\ngo anywhere together on the slightest whim、\njust to see what destiny had in store.
Until a certain chance encounter、 however、\nneither of them had ever even considered\nreturning to Dogi's homeland.
'Look over there、 in the distance-- you can\nsee Felghana from here!'、 Dogi exclaimed. He\nwas pointing past the shore、 over the ocean.
Adol fixed his eyes on the horizon、 where he\nsaw a vague outline of Dogi's birthplace. It\nseemed far、 but still well within reach.
Their goal was set three months prior when a\ncaravan of traveling merchants visited the\ntown they happened to be passing through.
This particular caravan had coincidentally\ncrossed Adol and Dogi's path numerous times、\ndrawing quite a crowd on every occasion.
As soon as they'd unload and set up shop、\nthrongs of people would rush in to buy their\nexotic goods and hear tales of foreign lands.
On that fateful day、 Adol and Dogi were among\nthe throngs、 hoping to learn all they could\nfrom the worldliest visitors around.
Sadly、 the merchants had already been talking\nwith eager townsfolk for hours、 and seemed to\nhave tired of endlessly telling their tales.
With masses of curious onlookers nipping at\ntheir heels、 they began making sour faces and\ncomplaining loudly of their ill fortunes.
'We need to rest、 my friends! Before this、\nwe passed through a land called Felghana、\nwhere we worked hard but sold nothing!'
Perhaps feeling guilty at besmirching the\nname、 they continued、 addressing the tribu-\nlations being faced by the Felghanan people.
Apparently、 through strange weather and\nafflictions of unknown cause、 production of\ncrops had reached an all-time low.
As a result、 the cost of living had increased\nexorbitantly、 making the basic necessities of\nlife much harder to come by.
'Seemed true enough to us、' interjected one\nof the merchants. 'All the plants in the\nfields had an unhealthy yellowish hue.'
'But the peculiar thing is、 the trees in the\nnearby woods were all green and vibrant!'
'Something was clearly amiss. But certainly、\nunder such conditions、 who can blame them for\nnot buying our wares?'
'We quickly set out for greener pastures--\nquite literally、 in fact. And here we are、\nalbeit weary from the ordeal...'
As the merchants recovered from their bout of\nindiscretion、 they moved on to another topic.\nBut Dogi did not. He was clearly perturbed.
Adol did not notice this change in Dogi's\ncountenance、 however. He had become wholly\npreoccupied by the merchants' further tales.
It wasn't until later that night that Dogi\nfinally spoke up.
He revealed to Adol that he had been born and\nraised in Felghana、 in a small town called\nRedmont.
And after leaving Redmont to see the world\neight years prior、 he had never once returned\nto visit.
'I kept meaning to、' he said、 'but I just\nnever got around to it. And now、 it sounds\nlike they're really in trouble. Adol、 I--'
Adol put a finger to Dogi's lips、 cutting him\noff mid-sentence. No more needed to be said.\nWithout a word、 Adol nodded his consent.
Dogi's expression brightened instantly. In\nthat moment、 their next destination had\nbecome clear.
The following morning、 they were to set out\non a long journey to the town of Redmont、 in\nthe land of Felghana.
As the two of them made their way across\nEurope、 Dogi recounted tales of his boyhood、\npainting an image for Adol to envision.
'We've been to a lot of different towns、 and\nsome have been really gorgeous...but Redmont\ntrumps them all!
'The streets are filled with a warmth and\nenergy unlike anyplace else in the world、 and\nthe local fruits and crafts are the best.
'The people、 too、 are about the nicest you'll\never find. They'd give you the shirts off\ntheir backs if you needed them!
'I was actually orphaned at a young age、 so\nthe whole town basically raised me、 and I\nnever once felt lonely or anything.
'I always helped out at the inn、 and the\nowner there was kinda like my mother. She\nreally looked out for me.
'I was a bit of a menace、 though. Not too\nsurprising、 huh? I'd always go out and cause\ntrouble、 and drag all my friends into it!
'It's all coming back to me...the blacksmith、\nAdonis...the shopkeeper、 Cynthia...and the\nStoddart children at the mayor's house...
'Man、 they were little brats like me when I\nleft. Hard to imagine them all grown-up! I'll\nhave to make sure I stop in and say hi...'
After a brief pause、 Dogi added one last\ncomment.
'You know、 looking back...I'm really lucky to\nknow all the people I know. You included、\nAdol!'
Adol felt the same way、 and nodded his\nresponse to Dogi's compliment、 a modest\nsmile stretched across his face.
The two of them stared at Sienna Bay for just\na short while longer before walking down the\nhill、 toward the harbor.
The road into the port town was well-\nmaintained、 clearly intended for tourism\nand trade-- but it was also strangely empty.
As noontime approached、 a small group of\nhorse-drawn covered wagons crossed their\npath、 breaking the day's calming silence.
Each wagon was decorated with flags、 and\nthe passengers were adorned in unusually\ncolorful garments.
For Adol and Dogi、 this was a dead giveaway\nthat they'd encountered a gypsy caravan of\nfortune-tellers、 acrobats and such.
These were a nomadic people who had no home\noutside their own coaches、 and were most\nrenown for their highly accurate divination.
Dogi called out to one of the drivers、 and\nslowly、 the caravan came to a halt.
He asked them if they knew of the troubles in\nFelghana、 and they were indeed aware of the\nrumors...
...But sadly、 they knew no more than what\nthe traveling merchants had previously\nrevealed.
After conversing with them for a short while\nlonger、 Dogi suddenly had an idea. He looked\nover at Adol.
'Hey、 Adol、 what say we get our fortune told?\nMaybe we can find out what's causing all\nthe problems in Felghana that way!'
Adol nodded his approval、 and Dogi paid the\nfortune-teller.
She was a beautiful young woman with smooth、\nglossy black hair that tumbled all the way to\nthe small of her back.
Without a word、 she took a table from the\nback of her coach、 placed it along the road-\nside、 and centered a crystal ball upon it.
She then laid her hands on the ball and\nstared intently into its depths...
...And in no time at all、 it became clear\nthat the fortune-teller had borne witness to\nsomething most unholy therein.
As Adol、 Dogi and the other gypsies watched、\nher face gradually drained of color、 and her\neyes widened with panic.
Then、 small cracks began appearing along the\ncrystal's surface...
...And all at once、 it shattered out into\ninnumerable shards、 as if detonated from\nwithin!
The fortune-teller staggered back from the\nimpact、 looking like someone had punched her\nin the face...
...And then、 she collapsed in a heap upon\nthe ground.
Instantly、 the other gypsies rushed to her\naid、 administering to her wounds. It took\nlittle time for her to regain consciousness.
But even back in the safety of the caravan、\nfar from danger、 she would not say one word\nabout the horrors she had witnessed.
Each time the subject was broached、 her\nface would contort in an expression of\npure、 uncontrollable、 almost primal terror.
She would not even speak of other topics--\nshe simply said nothing at all for several\nminutes.
Then、 she gestured for one of the acrobats to\ncome over、 and whispered a few words to him.
Although loud enough for Adol and Dogi to\nhear、 it was not their language she spoke.\nThe acrobat nodded、 and approached Dogi.
Whatever the fortuneteller had seen、 it could\nnot be put into words lest it bring forth a\ncataclysm beyond imagining、 he said.
All he could add to this explanation was that\nAdol and Dogi should stay out of Felghana--\nand he quite vehemently stressed this point.
But to this、 Adol would not nod his consent.
He had known from the start that this was no\nmere vacation、 and had no intention of aban-\ndoning his journey out of fear alone.
Dogi was of the same mind、 and firmly shook\nhis head.
The acrobat sighed、 knowing he could no more\nconvince these two to stay behind than\nconvince a mountain to stroll away.
He returned their money、 then joined the rest\nof the caravan in bowing a polite farewell.\nThe group then made an overly hasty retreat.
Shortly thereafter、 Adol and Dogi arrived at\nthe nearby port town、 where they stayed the\nnight to recuperate from this unpleasantness.
The next morning、 they chartered a small boat\nand set off、 never looking back. And before\nlong、 their destination had come into view.
'Look、 Adol!'、 exclaimed Dogi. 'There it is!\nFelghana、 the land where I grew up! We're\ngetting really close now!'
The sun was hidden behind a mountain range\nfar in the distance、 dyeing the earth and sky\nalike an eerie shade of crimson.
Still、 Adol could see the land growing ever\nnearer. As he stared、 he couldn't help but\nthink of that poor fortune-teller...
Dogi、 on the other hand、 had a wide-eyed、\nchildlike expression on his face. 'It's as\nbeautiful as I remember、' he said glowingly.
Adol simply nodded in silence、 never once\nturning his gaze from the ever-encroaching\nmass of twilight-hued land before them.
